subskill: Two pricing plans identical at one k; spread of k
prompt: Plan A charges k dollars per item plus a $6 setup fee. Plan B charges $3 per item plus a design fee of 2k dollars. Here k is a whole number from 1 to 50. For some values of k, there is an order of n items, where n is a positive whole number, for which the two plans charge the same total, and that total is between $40 and $70, inclusive. What is the difference between the greatest and least such values of k?
explanation: For an order of n items, Plan A costs kn + 6 and Plan B costs 3n + 2k. Setting them equal: kn - 3n = 2k - 6, so (k - 3)n = 2(k - 3). Treat k = 3 as its own case: then both plans cost 3n + 6 for every n, so they charge the same total for every order; an order of n = 12 costs $42, which is in the band, so k = 3 qualifies. For k ≠ 3 we may divide by k - 3: the plans agree only at n = 2, where the total is 2k + 6. That total is from 40 to 70 when 17 ≤ k ≤ 32. So the qualifying values are k = 3 and k = 17 through 32; the greatest is 32 and the least is 3, a difference of 29. Choice 15 comes from dividing by k - 3 for every k, which loses k = 3 and gives 32 - 17. Choice 47 forgets that the plans meet at n = 2 and uses k + 3 as the common total, which puts the generic values at k = 37 through 50. Choice 17 uses the per-item price 3 as the order size, so the common total is taken as 3(k + 3), giving k = 11 through 20 together with k = 3.
solve: const ok=[]; for(let k=1;k<=50;k++){ let hit=false; for(let n=1;n<=200;n++){ const A=k*n+6, B=3*n+2*k; if(A===B && A>=40 && A<=70){ hit=true; break } } if(hit) ok.push(k) } return Math.max(...ok)-Math.min(...ok)

distractor_solve.15: const ok=[]; for(let k=1;k<=50;k++){ const t=2*k+6; if(t>=40&&t<=70) ok.push(k) } return Math.max(...ok)-Math.min(...ok)
distractor_solve.17: const ok=[3]; for(let k=1;k<=50;k++){ if(k===3) continue; const t=3*(k+3); if(t>=40&&t<=70) ok.push(k) } return Math.max(...ok)-Math.min(...ok)
distractor_solve.47: const ok=[3]; for(let k=1;k<=50;k++){ if(k===3) continue; const t=k+3; if(t>=40&&t<=70) ok.push(k) } return Math.max(...ok)-Math.min(...ok)

mechanism: k = 3 makes the plans identical (every n)
otherwise n = 2 and the total is 2k + 6
spread of the qualifying k including the identical case
quantity_asked: difference between the greatest and least whole-number k from 1 to 50 for which the plans charge the same total, between $40 and $70, for some order

setup.i: k is the per-item price of one plan and also multiplies the other plan's fixed fee, so at one k the two cost models are identical
setup.ii: the plans charge the same total for some whole-number order, with that total in a stated band
setup.iii: difference between the greatest and least qualifying k

plugback.why: The key is at natural try 3 ascending. The asked quantity is a spread over qualifying k, which no single option can be substituted into; checking an option needs the whole qualifying set, including whether k = 3 counts.

15.why: Dividing by k - 3 for every k drops the identical-plans case; dropping a value narrows the spread only if it was an endpoint, and the stem does not show where k = 3 lies relative to the generic band.

17.why: Using the per-item price 3 as the order size changes the common total to 3(k + 3) and moves the band down; the stem gives no reason to expect a narrower or wider spread.

47.why: Taking k + 3 as the common total moves the generic band to the top of the range; whether that widens or narrows the spread depends on the range end and on k = 3, which the stem does not compare.

intermediate_check: 15: it is the spread of the generic band; the key does not follow from it through one printed relation (it needs the unprinted k = 3 and the band top). 47: no; a different band. 17: no; a different band. None is one printed step from 29.
shape_check: Properties handed over: the spread is a whole number from 0 to 49 (all four survive); no parity or cap. All four survive together.
interior_parity_check: Middle values 17 and 29: both two-digit integers of complexity 2; the key 29 is not the cleaner one.
arith_class_check: 15, 17, 29 and 47 are all odd; the key is not alone in any class.

self_audit.note: A test-wise student sets the totals equal, gets (k - 3)n = 2(k - 3) and will usually cancel to n = 2; the decision point is that k = 3 makes the plans identical. Covering the work, all four options remain legal from the stem alone. Natural try 3: the key is not at try 1-2, and in any case a spread over k cannot be checked from an option. The bypass option 15 is exactly what skipping this item's decision point gives: dividing by k - 3 for every k, so the identical plans at k = 3 are lost and the spread is 32 - 17. (read) lines answered: PAIR 29 - 17 = 12 = 2 x printed 6; DPAIR/DSUM 29 + 17 = 46 = 6 + 40 and 29 + 47 = 76 = 6 + 70. No student adds two options to compare with the fee plus a band end, and 12 is the gap between two different bands, not a doubled fee. Read and judged harmless.
